This research analyzes the formation and growth of price bubbles in the marine freight industry by using the Supremum Augmented Dickey-Fuller (SADF) and Generalized Supremum Augmented Dickey-Fuller (GSADF) econometric methods, utilizing data from the Baltic Dry Index (BDI). The study covers the timeframe from the 47th week of 2019 to the 51st week of 2023. Research indicates the presence of eight separate pricing bubbles in the marine industry worldwide during this period. Quarterly, the distribution of bubbles was as follows: one in Q1 2020, one in Q2 2021, two in Q4 2021, one in Q1 2022, and one each in Q1, Q3, and Q4 of 2023. Significantly, six of these bubbles appeared before the World Health Organization declared that COVID-19 no longer represented a worldwide public health emergency. The emergence of these first bubbles is intricately linked to pandemic-related events, including heightened demand for raw materials, interruptions from lockdowns, impacts of economic recovery, and shortages of vessels. The latter two bubbles, seen after COVID, may be ascribed to logistical constraints at Brazilian ports and heightened cargo quantities of coal, iron ore, and bauxite.

Covid-19 pandemi dönemi denizcilik sektörü aç\u0131s\u0131ndan önemli uygulamalar\u0131n yap\u0131ld\u0131\u011f\u0131 ve sonuçlar\u0131n deneyimlendi\u011fi bir süreç olmu\u015ftur. Bu dönemde çe\u015fitli denizcilik piyasalar\u0131 üzerinde farkl\u0131 etkiler gözlemlenmi\u015ftir. Navlun piyasalar\u0131 pandemi öncesinden pandeminin ilk aylar\u0131n\u0131 takip eden döneme geçi\u015fte yo\u011funla\u015fan talep ve belirsizlik ortam\u0131n\u0131n etkisiyle h\u0131zla yükselen bir navlun oran\u0131 trendini deneyimlerken pandemi sonras\u0131 dönemde keskin dü\u015fü\u015fler ya\u015fam\u0131\u015ft\u0131r. Bu çal\u0131\u015fmada, navlun oranlar\u0131n\u0131n dalgal\u0131 bir seyir izledi\u011fi pandemi-öncesi, pandemi ve pandemi-sonras\u0131 dönemleri kapsayan 2019–2023 y\u0131llar\u0131na ait ayl\u0131k Baltic Dry Index (BDI) ve Shanghai Containerized Freight Index (SCFI) verileri kullan\u0131larak nicel, betimsel ve kesitsel bir ara\u015ft\u0131rma tasar\u0131m\u0131 benimsenmi\u015ftir. Be\u015f y\u0131ll\u0131k süreçte kuru yük ve konteyner navlun endeksleri aras\u0131ndaki ili\u015fki analiz edilmi\u015f; de\u011fi\u015fkenler aras\u0131ndaki etkile\u015fim Pearson ve Spearman korelasyon analizleri ile çoklu do\u011frusal regresyon analizi arac\u0131l\u0131\u011f\u0131yla incelenerek endeks de\u011ferleri aras\u0131ndaki ili\u015fki ortaya konulmu\u015ftur. Çal\u0131\u015fma sonucunda kuru yük endeksi ile konteyner navlun endeksi aras\u0131ndaki ili\u015fki tespit edilmi\u015f ve ç\u0131kar\u0131mlarda bulunulmu\u015ftur. Çal\u0131\u015fma kapsam\u0131nda ayr\u0131ca kuru yük endeksinin belli ba\u015fl\u0131 alt endeksleri ile konteyner navlun endeksi aras\u0131ndaki ili\u015fki analiz edilmi\u015f. Böylece konteyner navlun endeksinin hangi alt endekslerle ne düzeyde ili\u015fkisinin oldu\u011fu tespit edilmi\u015f ve buna yönelik ç\u0131kar\u0131mlar yap\u0131lm\u0131\u015ft\u0131r.

This research analyzes the formation and growth of price bubbles in the marine freight industry by using the Supremum Augmented Dickey-Fuller (SADF) and Generalized Supremum Augmented Dickey-Fuller (GSADF) econometric methods, utilizing data from the Baltic Dry Index (BDI). The study covers the timeframe from the 47th week of 2019 to the 51st week of 2023. Research indicates the presence of eight separate pricing bubbles in the marine industry worldwide during this period. Quarterly, the distribution of bubbles was as follows: one in Q1 2020, one in Q2 2021, two in Q4 2021, one in Q1 2022, and one each in Q1, Q3, and Q4 of 2023. Significantly, six of these bubbles appeared before the World Health Organization declared that COVID-19 no longer represented a worldwide public health emergency. The emergence of these first bubbles is intricately linked to pandemic-related events, including heightened demand for raw materials, interruptions from lockdowns, impacts of economic recovery, and shortages of vessels. The latter two bubbles, seen after COVID, may be ascribed to logistical constraints at Brazilian ports and heightened cargo quantities of coal, iron ore, and bauxite.

Covid-19 pandemi dönemi denizcilik sektörü açısından önemli uygulamaların yapıldığı ve sonuçların deneyimlendiği bir süreç olmuştur. Bu dönemde çeşitli denizcilik piyasaları üzerinde farklı etkiler gözlemlenmiştir. Navlun piyasaları pandemi öncesinden pandeminin ilk aylarını takip eden döneme geçişte yoğunlaşan talep ve belirsizlik ortamının etkisiyle hızla yükselen bir navlun oranı trendini deneyimlerken pandemi sonrası dönemde keskin düşüşler yaşamıştır. Bu çalışmada, navlun oranlarının dalgalı bir seyir izlediği pandemi-öncesi, pandemi ve pandemi-sonrası dönemleri kapsayan 2019–2023 yıllarına ait aylık Baltic Dry Index (BDI) ve Shanghai Containerized Freight Index (SCFI) verileri kullanılarak nicel, betimsel ve kesitsel bir araştırma tasarımı benimsenmiştir. Beş yıllık süreçte kuru yük ve konteyner navlun endeksleri arasındaki ilişki analiz edilmiş; değişkenler arasındaki etkileşim Pearson ve Spearman korelasyon analizleri ile çoklu doğrusal regresyon analizi aracılığıyla incelenerek endeks değerleri arasındaki ilişki ortaya konulmuştur. Çalışma sonucunda kuru yük endeksi ile konteyner navlun endeksi arasındaki ilişki tespit edilmiş ve çıkarımlarda bulunulmuştur. Çalışma kapsamında ayrıca kuru yük endeksinin belli başlı alt endeksleri ile konteyner navlun endeksi arasındaki ilişki analiz edilmiş. Böylece konteyner navlun endeksinin hangi alt endekslerle ne düzeyde ilişkisinin olduğu tespit edilmiş ve buna yönelik çıkarımlar yapılmıştır.

"https://doi.org/10.36811/gjpr.2019.110003", "metadata": {"title": "Mental distress in stroke rehabilitation", "doi": "10.36811/gjpr.2019.110003", "publication_date": "2019-04-10", "description": "

The most common psychological consequence is depression. Post-stroke depression may hinder rehabilitation and may exercise a negative effect on the course of the disease. In this study, changes were measured in joint function, activities of daily living (Functional Independence Measure and Barthel Index) and psychological state in our own patients.

Setting: Physiotherapy Center, Ss. Cosmas and Damian Rehabilitation Institute, Visegrád, Hungary.

Methodology: 30 clients who had suffered an ischaemic stroke and showed prevalent unilateral symptoms in the upper limbs were selected at random. Rehabilitation was started 10±3 days after the acute event. The following measurements were taken before and after rehabilitation: joint function (“global joint function” [%]), the functional independence measure (FIM), the Barthel Index, the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) and the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE). Changes in individual parameters due to treatments (paired t-test; p<0.05) were studied as well as correlations between joint function, activities of daily living and psychological state (correlation analysis; p<0.05).

Results: Significant changes were found due to treatments for all the parameters under investigation compared to the before-treatment state (joint function before treatment [BT]: 63.22%, after treatment [AT]: 93.41%; FIM BT: 89.83, AT: 118.4; Barthel Index BT: 61.36, AT: 88.8; BDI BT: 20.33, AT: 10.5; MMSE BT: 11.83, AT: 22.16; p<0.05). There were strong correlations (r) between changes in joint function, activities of daily living and psychological state (joint function and MMSE: 0.796; FIM and MMSE: 0.655; Barthel Index and MMSE: 0.601; joint function and BDI: -0.786; FIM and BDI: -0.685; Barthel Index and BDI: -0.623; p<0.05).

Conclusion: Based on our results, favourable changes in joint function and activities of daily living in the case of stroke rehabilitation are likely to have a positive effect on clients’ psychological state, thus improving their life changes.

Keywords: Stroke; Depression; Joint function; Activities of daily living
